survivors.claim: A collided AC-ID whose sibling owner is `status: superseded` is kept `open` forever, because the many-to-many rule treats only the literal `done` as done. This repo carries 20 such live collisions today (AC-20260908-01-1..8 and AC-20260908-05-1..12, each defined by a done spec and a superseded twin); the 25 citing tests are all invariant-kept anyway so the retire delta is zero, but in a host whose superseded twin's tests are not invariant-kept the rule cements a permanent over-keep. Pre-fix HEAD gives identical totals, so this is D3-literal behaviour the fix preserves, not a regression.

A spec file the directory walk can see but cannot read is silently skipped, so an unreadable implementing sibling contributes no owner record and the citing test retires — the one unknown D3's fail-safe intent does not fail safe on. Executed: A(done)+B(implementing, chmod 000) sharing an id retires the citing test under --all-done and --spec A. The Contracts block reserves exit 2 only for an unreadable root/specs dir or the --spec target, so this is a gap in the contract rather than a breach of it.

Any .md under specs/ carrying an `## Acceptance Criteria` heading with a well-formed bullet becomes a co-owner with status null and keeps the citing test open forever — e.g. a sidecar or notes file quoting an AC bullet. spec-number-check.js skips sidecars, so the gate never refuses it. No such file exists in this repo today.

The sidecar's fixture-repair paragraph says 'the six inline sites'; the diff holds seven inline pathspec staging lines outside the helper (close-refusals 3, merge-reentry 1, replay-record 1, stopped-row-durability 1, review-driver.test.js 1). The six FILES named are right; the site count is off by one.
